column1: # Every `data/*` release tag this repository has published, and the commit it
# Why this exists. The modelling repository pins a tag per fit: 79 of its fits
# name one of these, and two vintages were vendored, fitted against and
# overwritten before any commit of theirs captured them -- so for a period the
# reproducibility of those fits rested on a tag here continuing to exist. That
# makes tag immutability a property of the data contract rather than a habit,
# and a property nobody checks is a promise rather than a guarantee.
# What it asserts. Each tag below still exists and still resolves to the commit
# still_where_it_was` fails if one is deleted or moved, which is the only way a
# consumer's pinned vintage can become unreachable.
# NEVER edit or remove a row to make the check pass. A row that no longer
# resolves means a published tag moved, and the fix is to restore the tag, not
# to update the register to match the damage.
# `commit` is the commit the tag names -- the dereferenced target for an
# annotated tag, which all of these are.
# Naming. From 2026-09-01 the first release of a day is `-r0`; before that it
# is the bare `data/<date>`, and the bare form was read inconsistently even
# here (2026-08-15 runs bare, r2, r3 ... with no r1, so that day's bare tag
# stood for r1, while every other day's stood for r0). Historical tags are not
# renamed: they are what published fits point at.
